question.prompt: Name a scientist known for work in astronomy, astrophysics, or cosmology.
question.criteria: Any real scientist with documented research contributions to astronomy, astrophysics, or cosmology counts.

answers.evidence: Albert Einstein developed general relativity, a foundation of modern cosmology.
Stephen Hawking studied black holes and the origins of the universe.
Galileo Galilei made pioneering telescopic observations of the Moon, planets, and stars.
Isaac Newton developed laws of motion and universal gravitation that explained planetary motion.
Carl Sagan researched planetary atmospheres and helped popularize astronomy.
Neil deGrasse Tyson is an astrophysicist whose research has included star formation and the structure of the Milky Way.
Nicolaus Copernicus developed a heliocentric model in which Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun.
Johannes Kepler formulated three laws describing planetary motion.
Edwin Hubble established that galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way and studied the relationship between their distances and recession speeds.
Edmond Halley calculated the orbit and predicted the return of the comet now named after him.
Vera Rubin studied galaxy rotation and provided influential evidence for dark matter.
William Herschel discovered Uranus and conducted extensive surveys of stars and nebulae.
Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovered the first radio pulsars.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin established that stars are composed predominantly of hydrogen and helium.
Annie Jump Cannon developed a widely used system for classifying stars by their spectra.
Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar studied stellar structure and established a mass limit for white dwarf stars.
Georges Lemaître proposed an expanding universe and an early version of the Big Bang theory.
Jan Oort studied the Milky Way and proposed a distant reservoir of comets surrounding the solar system.
Tycho Brahe collected highly precise astronomical observations before the invention of the telescope.
Caroline Herschel discovered comets and contributed to astronomical catalogues.
Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the relationship between Cepheid variable stars’ pulsation periods and luminosities.
Arthur Eddington studied stellar structure and helped test general relativity through eclipse observations.
Fritz Zwicky inferred the presence of dark matter from the motions of galaxies in a galaxy cluster.
Beatrice Tinsley developed models explaining how galaxies evolve over time.
Meghnad Saha developed an ionization equation that helps explain the spectra of stars.
Ejnar Hertzsprung helped establish the relationship between stars’ temperatures and luminosities.

question.explanation: Valid answers include scientists who studied planets, stars, galaxies, gravity, and the universe’s origins and evolution—not just the examples listed here.
